item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Disclaimers

Disclaimers

Covers both Transformative Life Solutions and Transformative Leadership Systems.

What we do not provide

Through Transformative Life Solutions and Transformative Leadership Systems, we provide neutral ADR, conflict‑coaching, and organizational facilitation services only. We do not provide:

  • Legal advice
  • Legal representation
  • Legal advocacy
  • Medical or mental health counseling
  • Clinical therapeutic services

Confidentiality

Mediation‑related communication is confidential. Two statements of that commitment are set out below, from the practice's own guide and brief.

From the practice's website guide

In accordance with the Maryland Mediation and Confidentiality Act, all mediation‑related communication will remain confidential.

From the practice's brief

Per Maryland Rule 17, all communication with this ADR practice is confidential. Our practitioners cannot be compelled to disclose any mediation or arbitration communication in any judicial, administrative, or other proceeding, and such communications are not subject to discovery.

Professional Standards

Our practitioners abide by recognized professional standards for mediators, arbitrators, and conflict‑resolution professionals including the Maryland Standards of Conduct for Mediators and Maryland Uniform Arbitration Act (MUAA).

Terms of use

The terms that apply to using this website, including eligibility, fees, and liability, are set out separately.

Read the Terms of Use

FAQ

Common questions

What is the difference between mediation, arbitration, and med-arb?

In mediation, a neutral helps the parties reach their own agreement. In arbitration, a neutral hears each side and issues a decision that may be binding or non-binding, depending on what the parties agree to. Med-arb combines the two: mediation first, then arbitration for any issues that remain.

How much do arbitration, mediation, and negotiation support cost?

Fees depend on the process, the number of parties, and the time involved. We confirm pricing after screening, before anything is scheduled.

Do you work with consumer-facing companies?

No. If your matter involves a consumer transaction, or if you are a consumer‑facing company or organization, Transformative Leadership Systems cannot assist due to statutory ethics requirements under Maryland Public Ethics Law §5‑502.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Policies

Privacy policy

How we collect, use, and protect your information, across both practices.

Last updated: 22 September 2026

Who this policy covers

This policy covers lettlshelp.com and both practices on it: Transformative Life Solutions and Transformative Leadership Systems. Both are operated by Tanika L. Smith.

You can reach us by phone or text on (240) 650‑0007, or by email at LifeSolutions@LetTLSHelp.com or LeadershipSystems@LetTLSHelp.com.

The short version

This website does not run forms on its own server, set cookies, or store anything on your device. It does not track you, and we do not sell or rent your information.

What we do hold is what you choose to send us by email, text, or phone, plus the ordinary server records our web host keeps.

When you use a form on this site

The contact and screening forms do not submit to us over the web. When you press Send or Submit, the form opens your own email app with your answers already written into a message addressed to us. Nothing is sent until you press send in your email app.

This means your answers travel as an ordinary email, through your email provider and ours. Email is not encrypted end to end. If a matter is sensitive, call or text instead.

So that a long message is not lost if your email app shortens it, the form also copies your answers to your device's clipboard. They stay there until you copy something else. We never see your clipboard.

If your browser has no email app to open — which is common if you read your mail on the web — the page shows you the finished message so you can copy it into your own webmail. That text is only on your screen; it is not sent anywhere until you send it yourself.

Because the message is created inside your own email app, this website never receives or stores what you typed.

What we ask for, and what not to send

The forms ask for your name, email address, phone number, how you prefer to be contacted, and short answers about the kind of matter you have, so we can tell whether we are allowed to help.

Please do not send confidential details about your dispute before we confirm eligibility. The forms say so at the point where it matters.

Information collected automatically

Our web host keeps standard server logs: the IP address you connect from, your browser and device type, which pages you requested, and when. These are used to keep the site running and secure, and we do not use them to build a profile of you.

Typefaces served by Google

The site's typefaces load from Google Fonts. To deliver them, Google receives your IP address and basic browser information. Google does not set cookies for this, and we send Google nothing else about you.

Cookies, analytics, and tracking

This site sets no cookies, uses no browser storage, and has no analytics, advertising, or social media tracking installed. That is why you are not asked to accept cookies.

If we add analytics later, we will update this policy and say plainly what is collected before it goes live.

Screening records

We keep a record of screening decisions, including matters we cannot accept and the reason, because our ethics obligations require us to document them.

Who else sees your information

Your email reaches our email provider, and our website is served by our web host. We do not share your information with anyone else except where the law requires it.

We do not sell, rent, or trade personal information, and we never have.

Your choices

You can ask us what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Email or call us and we will respond.

We may need to keep screening records even after a request to delete, where our ethics obligations require it.

Children

This website is meant for adults and is not directed to children under 13. We do not knowingly collect information from children.

Changes to this policy

If we change how the site handles information, we will update this page and change the date at the top. Significant changes will be described here rather than made quietly.

item.dc:creator: admin

Policies

Terms of use

These terms cover this website and both practices on it.

Last updated: 22 September 2026

About these terms

These terms apply to lettlshelp.com and to both practices on it. By using the site, you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

What this website is

The site describes our alternative dispute resolution services and helps you find out whether we can help. It is general information only.

Nothing here is legal advice, and nothing here is medical or mental health advice. Do not act or delay acting on something you read here without getting proper advice for your own situation.

Using the site does not make you a client

Reading these pages, sending a form, or emailing or calling us does not by itself create a client relationship. A relationship begins only when we have screened your matter, both sides have agreed to work together, and any agreement we ask for is in place.

Eligibility and screening

Every matter is screened before we accept it, in writing and by conversation. We cannot accept matters that fall outside what our ethics rules allow, including consumer matters and matters involving consumer‑facing businesses.

If we cannot help, we will provide free supportive referrals. Those referrals are suggestions, not a recommendation of any particular organization or an endorsement of the advice they may give.

What we do not provide

We provide neutral ADR, conflict‑coaching, and organizational facilitation services only. We do not provide legal advice, legal representation, or legal advocacy, and we do not provide medical or mental health counseling or clinical therapeutic services.

You may wish to have your own attorney review any agreement reached in mediation.

Confidentiality

Mediation‑related communication is treated as confidential. The Disclaimers page sets out the standards we work to.

Messages you send us

Messages sent from this site go through your own email app, so they travel as ordinary email and are not encrypted end to end. Please do not send confidential details about a dispute before we confirm we can help. If a matter is sensitive, call or text us.

We cannot guarantee that an email reaches us, so if you do not hear back, please phone.

Fees, scheduling, and cancellations

Services are provided for a fee. Cancellation charges may apply. Please read your agreements and contracts carefully.

Our content

The text, logos, and design of this site belong to us and may not be copied or reused commercially without permission. You are welcome to print or share pages for your own personal use.

Links to other sites

Where we link to another organization, such as a referral, we do so for convenience. We do not control those sites and are not responsible for their content, accuracy, or privacy practices.

Availability

We try to keep the site accurate and available, but we cannot promise it will always be up to date or free of interruptions or errors.

Changes and contact

We may update these terms. The date at the top of the page shows when they last changed. Questions about these terms can go to either practice address or to our phone number.

Family and parenting mediation, interpersonal mediation, workplace and organizational facilitation for non-consumer-facing organizations, and one-on-one conflict coaching.

Do you offer divorce mediation and help with parenting plans?

Yes. Family and parenting mediation supports separation, parenting plans, co-parenting communication, and family transitions.

Can mediation help with a separation agreement or prenuptial agreement?

Mediation can help both people talk through the terms they want to reach. We do not provide legal advice or representation, so you may wish to have your own attorney review any agreement.

Do you provide legal advice?

No. Transformative Life Solutions provides mediation services only. We do not provide legal advice, legal representation, or legal advocacy.

Is this counseling or therapy?

No. We provide coaching and training services only. We do not provide medical or mental health counseling services.

Is mediation confidential?

In accordance with the Maryland Mediation and Confidentiality Act, all mediation-related communication will remain confidential. The full statement, with both wordings, is on the Disclaimers page.

What matters do you not handle?

We do not handle consumer-business disputes (such as refunds, billing, purchases, warranties, or service agreements), auto sales or repair disputes, home improvement or contractor disputes, housing disputes, or any matter connected to Maryland consumer protection laws or the Office of the Attorney General.

What happens if my matter isn't a fit?

We use written and verbal screening to determine eligibility. If we are unable to facilitate your matter, we will provide free supportive referrals.

Do you meet virtually or in person?

Both. We serve clients with virtual and in-person options.

Do you offer arbitration, negotiation support, or help with NDAs?

Arbitration, med-arb, and negotiation support for eligible, non-consumer-facing organizations are offered through our sister practice, Transformative Leadership Systems.

How do I get started?

Complete our online screening, email LifeSolutions@LetTLSHelp.com, or call or text (240) 650-0007.

How much does mediation cost?

Fees depend on the service and the time involved. We confirm pricing with you after screening, before any session is scheduled.

How long does mediation take?

It depends on the number of issues and how prepared both people are. We give you an estimate after screening.

What happens in a first mediation session?

The mediator explains the process and ground rules, each person describes what matters most to them, and together you set an agenda for the issues to work through.

Do both people have to agree to mediation?

Yes. All parties must agree to participate, unless an order requires it. If the other person has not agreed yet, you can still complete the screening and we will discuss next steps.

Do I still need a lawyer if we mediate?

We provide mediation only and do not give legal advice or representation, so many people choose to get independent legal advice about their options and to review anything they sign. Whether you need a lawyer is your decision.

Is a mediated agreement legally binding?

Mediation helps you and the other person reach terms you both accept. Whether those terms become legally enforceable depends on how they are written, signed, and, in some matters, submitted to a court. Because we do not provide legal advice, you may wish to have your own attorney review any agreement.

What if there has been abuse, violence, or safety concerns?

Tell us during screening. We ask directly about threats, violence, harassment, and coercive control. Depending on the circumstances we may still be able to help, may suggest a different structure, or may refer you elsewhere. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

How does divorce or separation mediation work?

Instead of arguing positions through others, both people meet with a neutral mediator to talk through the decisions a separation requires, such as parenting time, communication, and next steps. You control the outcome; the mediator manages the conversation and keeps it balanced.

What is a parenting plan?

A parenting plan is a written arrangement covering how co-parents share time, make decisions, handle holidays and exchanges, and communicate with each other. Mediation gives both parents a structured way to build one together.

item.content:encoded:
FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Clear answers about eligibility, processes, and boundaries.

What services does Transformative Leadership Systems offer?

Arbitration and med-arb (business-to-business only), business and organizational mediation, negotiation support, and conflict coaching for leaders.

What is the difference between mediation, arbitration, and med-arb?

In mediation, a neutral helps the parties reach their own agreement. In arbitration, a neutral hears each side and issues a decision that may be binding or non-binding, depending on what the parties agree to. Med-arb combines the two: mediation first, then arbitration for any issues that remain.

Who is eligible?

Non-consumer-facing business owners, nonprofit organizations, and professional entities. Typical matters include internal workplace disputes, leadership and partnership conflicts, board governance issues, and vendor–supplier disputes between non-consumer-facing entities.

Can you help with NDAs or other business contracts?

Negotiation support includes contract interpretation for non-consumer agreements and inter-organizational communication. We remain neutral and do not provide legal advice, so each party may wish to consult its own attorney.

Do you work with consumer-facing companies?

No. If your matter involves a consumer transaction, or if you are a consumer‑facing company or organization, Transformative Leadership Systems cannot assist due to statutory ethics requirements under Maryland Public Ethics Law §5‑502.

Do you provide legal advice?

No. We provide neutral ADR services only. We do not provide legal advice, legal representation, or legal advocacy.

Is this counseling or therapy?

No. We provide conflict-coaching and organizational facilitation services only. We do not provide medical or mental health counseling or clinical therapeutic services.

Is the process confidential?

All mediation‑related communication will remain confidential in accordance with applicable ADR confidentiality standards.

What happens if my matter isn't eligible?

We use written and verbal screening to determine eligibility and document every screening decision. If we are unable to facilitate your matter, we will provide free supportive referrals.

Do you meet virtually or in person?

Both. We serve eligible B2B clients with virtual and in-person options.

Do you handle family or personal conflicts?

Family, parenting, and interpersonal matters are handled by our sister practice, Transformative Life Solutions.

How do I get started?

Complete our online screening, email LeadershipSystems@LetTLSHelp.com, or call or text (240) 650-0007.

How much do arbitration, mediation, and negotiation support cost?

Fees depend on the process, the number of parties, and the time involved. We confirm pricing after screening, before anything is scheduled.

Who pays for the process?

Organizations commonly share the cost, though the parties can agree on a different split, and a contract clause may already say who pays.

How long does a business mediation or arbitration take?

It depends on the complexity of the dispute, the number of parties, and how much documentation is involved. We give you an estimate after screening.

What happens in the first session?

We confirm the process the parties have agreed to, set ground rules and confidentiality expectations, identify the issues in dispute, and agree on what information is needed to move forward.

Is an arbitration award binding?

That depends on what the parties agreed to. We offer binding, non-binding, and hybrid processes, so the agreement or contract clause that brings you to arbitration determines the effect of the outcome.

What is a mediation or arbitration clause in a contract?

It is a term in a business agreement saying that if a dispute arises, the parties will use mediation or arbitration rather than going straight to court. If your contract already has one, bring it to screening so we can confirm the process it requires.

How is arbitration different from going to court?

Arbitration is private, generally faster, and scheduled around the parties rather than a court docket, and the parties choose their neutral. Court proceedings are public and follow the court's rules and calendar.

Can you help with a partnership dispute or a board conflict?

Yes, for eligible non-consumer-facing organizations. We work with internal workplace disputes, leadership and partnership conflicts, board governance issues, and vendor–supplier disputes between non-consumer-facing entities.
